title: MeMCISA: Memristor-Enabled Memory-Centric Instruction-Set Architecture for Database Workloads
problem: Modern database systems require support for diverse and complex workloads including vector aggregation, convolution, and N-hop neighborhoods computing. Existing memory-centric computing architectures focus on AI or can only handle limited standalone queries like SORT and JOIN, lacking efficient support for these diverse database workloads.
motivation: Memory-centric computing architectures can significantly enhance database operation efficiency through higher compute parallelism and reduced data movement.
method: MeMCISA uses multiple separate banks of memristors (electronic elements that store data and perform computations) with computing circuits placed near each bank, enabling calculations to happen right at the storage level. It executes instructions in parallel whenever their input data is ready, not in fixed sequence (out-of-order scheduling), using four categories of operations: single-bit operations, element-by-element operations, vector operations on groups of data, and control instructions. The system automatically manages dependencies—when one operation needs the result of an earlier one—including complex vector patterns where one group-operation feeds into another, which traditional single-number instruction sets cannot handle efficiently. This allows the system to handle diverse database tasks like vector aggregation, convolution, and computing multi-hop paths through data.
key_novelty: The key innovation is using out-of-order scheduling (executing operations whenever their input data is ready) with vector instructions (operations on groups of values) on memristor-based multi-bank storage, enabling databases to efficiently compute the complex, interdependent calculations they perform without requiring strict instruction sequencing.
contributions: MeMCISA architecture with scalable multi-bank memristor-based storage and near-memory computing organization
Out-of-order scheduling scheme with vector instruction set (bit-level, element-level, vector-level, control-level instructions)
Data dependency handling mechanisms for vector scenarios in memory-centric architectures
Software-hardware co-designed framework enabling end-to-end simulation of database workloads on reconfigurable MeMCISA prototype
primary_theme: Memristor-based vector architecture for database acceleration
